text:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: GPU pool 'inference-west-1' reporting sustained saturation and a spike in 429 throttles. Autoscaler has not increased capacity in 8m. Queue depth growing. Paging on-call (sam).

sam: acked. grabbing metrics now. I see GPU utilization at 99% for the last 10m and the request queue length up ~4x. 429 rate for client-tier 'standard' spiked from 0.2% to 22%.

maya: tagging in — looks like autoscaler logs show repeated failed scale-ups: "max_nodes_reached" followed by "scaling_disabled_by_policy" (snippet below).

maya: ```
[2026-06-02T14:03:12Z] autoscaler: desired_replicas=12 current=8 -> attempting scale up
[2026-06-02T14:03:12Z] autoscaler: scale request rejected: max_nodes_reached (pool_limit=8)
[2026-06-02T14:03:12Z] routing: fallback to burst pool: none available
```

jordan: that max_nodes_reached is suspicious — dedicated reservations shouldn't be touched here. could be a recent policy change on pool caps. who pushed the policy?

lee: I rolled out a policy patch last night to enforce regional hard caps for cost control. It prevents autoscaler from exceeding pool_limit. I didn't expect it to hit these pools yet.

sam: ok, live mitigation plan: 1) temporarily lift pool cap to allow immediate scale, 2) prioritize production-paying tiers, 3) tune token-bucket so low-priority dev-tier gets throttled harder, 4) start evacuation of long-running background jobs. Who can lift the cap?

lee: I can revert the cap. Doing a quick rollback to previous policy now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: policy-revert (lee) — roll id: p-9421. Canary 0/3 -> 1/3.

maya: meanwhile, we observed token-bucket misconfiguration: for a recent routing change, the token bucket was applied at the global GPU pool level instead of per-tenant. That means a heavy tenant could consume tokens and starve others, causing throttles (429s) across the pool.

toni: confirming — logs show bucket_consume events tied to tenant_id=acct-84 with huge burst usage at 14:05:02.

sam: priority: prevent customer impact. Actions: A) patch token-bucket to per-tenant scope, B) apply emergency per-tenant rate caps for standard/free tiers, C) lift autoscale cap. Maya/Lee/Toni own A/B/C.

maya: working on per-tenant token-bucket patch. I'll prepare a hotfix config and test on canary routing. Expect ~5-7m.

lee: policy revert canary green. Deploy success: policy-revert (lee) roll id: p-9421 succeeded. Pool cap removed. Autoscaler now allowed to scale up.

sam: monitoring node count... new nodes coming up, but we need to avoid repeated queue thrashing — ramp autoscale faster but with cooldown to avoid flapping. Jordan can you adjust autoscaler params?

jordan: increasing max_replicas to 16 and reducing scale_cooldown to 60s for this pool. Patching cluster autoscaler config now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: autoscaler-config-change (jordan) — roll id: a-7834.

deploy-bot: Deploy finished: autoscaler-config-change (jordan) — success.

sam: telemetry: queue length dropping, 429s falling from 22% -> 3% in last 6m. Good trend.

toni: token-bucket hotfix applied to canary routing. Patch: scope set to per_tenant and burst reduced for free tier. Snippet: ```token_bucket: { scope: tenant, refill_rate: 250, burst: 1000 }```

maya: hotfix validated on canary. Rolling to full pool now.

deploy-bot: Deploy started: token-bucket-hotfix (maya) — roll id: t-5592.

cs-team: CS: we have two customers reporting degraded quality — CS ticket 98421 and 98422. Notifying them of mitigation steps and ETA.

sam: progress update for PagerDuty: 15m in, autoscaler added 6 nodes, token-bucket fixed, per-tenant rate limiting enforcing. Estimated time to full recovery: 10-15m.

lee: note — we still have some long-running inference jobs occupying GPUs. Initiating graceful preemption of background batch jobs (non-prod flagged).

jordan: preemption script running. Commands: ```kubectl label job batch-* preemptible=true && kubectl delete pod -l preemptible=true --grace-period=30```

sam: continued monitoring: 429s now at 0.8% and queue length near baseline. We'll keep watchers on for an hour.

toni: root cause summary (preliminary): 1) regional pool cap enforced by recent policy prevented autoscaler from adding capacity, 2) token-bucket misconfiguration applied globally allowed tenant-level bursts to exhaust shared tokens, 3) combined resulted in request queue growth and 429 throttles.

maya: immediate remediations completed. Next steps: post-incident audit of policy rollout process, add automated e2e test that validates autoscaler can scale beyond caps for emergency, and add unit tests for token-bucket scoping.

sam: handing off to night on-call (toni) — please monitor for 2 hours and verify CS tickets updated. I'll prepare the incident timeline and draft postmortem.

toni: on-call ack. I'll keep a heartbeat update every 30m. First one at +30m.

cs-team: updated customers with mitigation note and expected follow-up postmortem.

inc-bot: Incident annotated: severity=sev2, impact=partial (some standard-tier customers experienced elevated 429s), started=1764209876, mitigated=1764213098, handler=sam, follow_up="postmortem required; owners: eng-sre, eng-runtime, product"

sam: closing notes — lessons: avoid global token buckets on shared pools, ensure policy rollouts have safety gates that block hard caps without staged checks, and improve alerting to tie 429 rate to autoscaler rejection events. I'll post the draft postmortem in #postmortems in ~1h. :thumbsup:

toni: thanks team. I'll escalate to infra leads if we see regression.
